newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico/US cross-border canal plan dealt setback.
newsitem.headline: Mexico/US cross-border canal plan dealt setback.

text.p: A Mexican Senate panel urged the government of northern state Tamaulipas on Tuesday to suspend a $756 million plan to build a coastal canal that would provide a shipping link with the State of Texas.
The panel argued the plan suffered from several administrative oversights and would cause serious ecological damage on both sides of the border.
"The plan has serious environmental drawbacks which the authorities should thoroughly look into," Senate Ecology Committee member Carmen Bolado told reporters.
The 270-mile (436-km) canal would link ports in Tamaulipas, on the Gulf of Mexico, to 28,000 miles (45,000 km) of waterways in the United States via Brownsville, Texas.

The project would take advantage of natural canals between the main coastline and thin strips of land that run along the coast of southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. But Mexico would have to dig out new canals to extend the waterway as far south as the port of Tampico.

Bolado, of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), said the Ecology Ministry had raised 93 objections to the plan "which will be difficult to overcome," and said funds were also lacking with which to build the canal.
Furthermore, Bolado revealed a letter dated July 17 from Texas Governor George Bush Jr. to his opposite number in Tamaulipas, Manuel Cavazos, saying he could not back the plan.
"The intercoastal canal is a still-born project," she said.
